prompt: Holding an arrow key on the canvas should keep nudging the selection for as long as the key is held, by the usual 1 px a step, or 10 px with Shift. However long I hold the key, one Undo should take the whole hold back and put the layers where they were before I pressed it. Letting go of the key ends that step, and pressing it again starts a new one.

visibleIn.text: commands without a gesture id stay apart however close in time
True for the auto-repeat presses while a key is held

reference: The first press of an arrow key takes a gesture id, its repeats reuse it, and releasing the key drops it.

naive.summary: Merges a key repeat into the previous nudge when it comes within 400 ms by the editor clock, so a hold whose repeats pause becomes several entries.

note: Was B-P4 (proof-only, R4). Reclassified before any run: KeyEvent.repeat, the unused release() hook, ctx.newGesture() and a test that states gesture-id merging make R4 visible in the code. Its naive patch (a 400 ms window by the editor clock) stays as the check that the constraint catches a time window.
